content.text:
**Finding submitted: T4C — missing (high severity), preferred target.**

**What I checked**
- §9 (Termination) in full: 9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer's immediate cause-based rights, 9.5 non-cross-termination — there is no 9.4 and no convenience right for either party.
- Full-document searches for "for convenience", "without cause", "any reason", "early termination fee", "penalty" and every instance of "terminate": the only other exits are cause- or event-based (6.2 acceptance failure, 19.4 warranty, 27.3 force majeure) and non-renewal under 8.2.
- Term and commitment context: 8.1 fixes a three-year term; 2.1 makes the USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; 10.2 already refunds prepaid recurring Fees for the post-termination period.

**Why it fails fallback**
Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is expressly walk-away territory, so no fallback element (60–90 days' notice, capped fee, end-of-term Vendor right) can be met. Vendor holds no convenience right, so nothing being flagged benefits us.

**The change (one insertion, new §9.4)**
Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term — opened with a Section 2.1 override so the exit is operative. The take-or-pay volume commitment itself is left to the minimum-commitment rule, and the comment offers the 60–90 day / three-month fee-cap fallback.
